notes: Grey Matter: a monochrome digital broadsheet about the halftone dot. One procedurally generated dune landscape is drawn with canvas noise and screened four ways: a live round-dot halftone with screen angle, dot pitch and dot-gain controls plus a 3x loupe, Floyd-Steinberg dithering in the same frame, and a triptych comparing Bayer 4x4, Floyd-Steinberg and Atkinson at 360 px. Also includes an SVG two-screen moire demonstration, real footnote links, a print stylesheet that flips the dark chapter back to ink on paper, keyboard-operable controls and reduced-motion support. No image files, webfonts, libraries, analytics or external requests; everything is HTML, one CSS file and one script. Known limits: type falls back to each operating system's serif and mono faces, so letterforms differ by platform; the plate re-renders on resize and is drawn at CSS resolution rather than per-device-pixel for speed; the landscape is fixed rather than seedable; tested in Chromium (desktop and 390 px mobile) with print media emulation, not yet in Safari or Firefox.
